thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Spike detected: elevated 5xx + 429 rates on /v1/generate (us-west-2). 5xx pct = 11.8% over last 3m, 429s up ~8x. Trigger: error-rate > 5% and quota-throttle events rising. PagerDuty: paged oncall. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/1789002345 :rotating_light:
Jia (oncall): I'm on. seeing the alert. pulling up traces and recent deploys. anyone touching rate-limiter config in last 20m?
Omar (sre): I can see a config push to rate-limiter service 12m ago by marco@eng-runtime. Ruleset: per-tenant hard cap enforcement enabled (enforce=true) for pool "model-pool-A". Logs show large number of 429 -> gateway timeouts downstream.
Marco (eng-runtime): that was me, quick change to tighten soft-limit windows for burst protection. I thought it'd be safe. Rolling back now.
Jia (oncall): thanks. Marco, can you paste the rollback command you used? I'll start traffic mitigation (route + increase soft quota) while you revert.
Marco (eng-runtime): running rollback:
```
PATCH /internal/rate-limiter/config HTTP/1.1
Host: rl-control.us-west-2.internal
Authorization: Bearer ***
Content-Type: application/json

{"pool":"model-pool-A","enforce":false,"burst_window_ms":1000}
```
Response: 200 OK, config applied.
Omar (sre): after rollback I still see 429s in the next minute; looks like tokens exhausted and downstream caches still cold. We should open a bypass route to pool-B and increase fallback capacity.
Jia (oncall): executing traffic shift: enabling routing rule to prefer model-pool-B for non-SLA traffic. Command:
```
POST /internal/router/override
{"selector":"/v1/generate","priority":"low","target":"model-pool-B","duration_sec":600}
```
Router response: ok. Flushing connection pools to clear queued requests.
Nina (support): I've got three paying customers (acme, beta-inc, omega) on support threads reporting timeouts and 5xx since ~06:02. Acme says they saw "internal server error" on 12% of requests. ETA for mitigation?
Jia (oncall): immediate ETA: 10-15m for visible decrease after rollback + route shift. Provide update to customers now. Nina, please post interim status: "We are aware of degraded response rates for text generation endpoints; engineering is actively mitigating. Expect updates within 15 minutes."
Nina (support): posting now. I'll include link to status page and mention possible impact to background jobs.
Omar (sre): digging into metrics. Quick query (internal):
```
SELECT tenant_id, count(*) as errors, error_type
FROM request_logs
WHERE timestamp > now() - interval '10 minutes'
AND (status like '5%%' OR status=429)
GROUP BY tenant_id, error_type
ORDER BY errors desc
LIMIT 10;
```
Query result (truncated):
```
tenant acme: 142 errors (5xx)
tenant gamma: 98 errors (429)
tenant beta-inc: 34 errors (5xx)
```
Omar (sre): acme and gamma most impacted. gamma is hitting quota limits heavily — suggests misapplied per-tenant cap.
Marco (eng-runtime): I can temporarily bump soft quota for tenants flagged as critical and relax enforcement window. Running:
```
PATCH /internal/tenant/quota/gamma
{"soft_limit":2000, "enforce":false}
```
Response: 200. Also increasing global connection pool for pool-B by +30%.
Jia (oncall): monitoring traces. Error rate dropping: 5xx now 6.1%, 429s down ~50% since route change. Still above baseline but trending down.
incident-bot: Update: alert threshold cleared for 5xx (now 3.8%) but 429s still elevated (4.2%). Tracking as INCIDENT-1789002345.
Marco (eng-runtime): note — the original change tightened the client token bucket too aggressively and didn't account for warmup. My bad. We'll add a pre-check in deploy pipeline.
Nina (support): Customer comms posted. acme replied: "Thanks, we see improvements but background jobs still failing occasionally."
Omar (sre): next step: enable short-term caching for repeated prompt prefixes (apply KV prefix cache) to reduce burst load. Command:
```
POST /internal/serving/cache/apply
{"pool":"model-pool-A","cache_ttl_ms":5000,"mode":"prefix"}
```
Response: accepted.
Jia (oncall): good. I'm going to escalate to oncall-next for post-mitigation handoff. Liz, you're up in 15m. Summary: rate-limiter rollback + route to pool-B + per-tenant soft quota bumps + prefix caching applied. Residual errors decreasing.
Liz (oncall-next): ack, I'll monitor from 07:30 UTC and take ownership. Please leave any outstanding runbook items in the thread.
Omar (sre): creating incident timeline and preliminary impact:
- start 06:01 UTC: spikes begin
- 06:03 UTC: PagerDuty fired
- 06:05 UTC: config change to rate-limiter (tighten) by eng-runtime
- 06:14 UTC: rollback applied by eng-runtime
- 06:16 UTC: routing override to pool-B
- 06:20 UTC: per-tenant soft quota bumps for top impacted tenants
- 06:25 UTC: caching applied
- 06:28 UTC: 5xx < 5%
Customer impact summary: ~2% of requests for top customers returned 5xx or timeout, around 12k requests affected across multiple tenants in 30m window.
Nina (support): adding customer impact numbers to incident ticket and sending targeted follow-ups to acme and gamma.
Marco (eng-runtime): action items for postmortem: revert riskier rate-limiter changes from quick deploy flow, add canary on quota changes, and add automatic rollback if 429 or 5xx spike detected within 5 minutes.
Jia (oncall): agreed. Also: immediate change — add a safeguard to block enforce=true from auto-apply without manual approval. Marco, please open PR and tag me.
Marco (eng-runtime): will do. PR link: https://git.redwood/internal/eng-runtime/pulls/4321
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigation in progress -> stable degraded. Incident owner: Jia. Next update scheduled in 30 minutes.
Liz (oncall-next): taking over monitoring. If anything spikes again, escalate to SRE rotation. Leaving detailed notes in incident ticket.
Jia (oncall): handing off. thanks team.
Nina (support): posting final customer update: "Mitigations are in place. We continue to monitor; engineering is working on permanent fixes. We will follow up with post-incident summary." :white_check_mark:
